name: Keep Alive (Request)
desc: Server sends a keep-alive ID that the client must echo back in C00PacketKeepAlive.

fields.name: id
fields.desc: Random keep-alive ID to echo back

writeup.p: S00PacketKeepAlive is the clientbound half of the play-state liveness probe. NetHandlerPlayServer sends it roughly once per second from its update loop with a server-chosen int key (field_147378_h), and the vanilla client echoes it back as C00PacketKeepAlive with the same key. NetHandlerPlayServer.processKeepAlive compares the echoed key and folds the round-trip into the player's ping EMA: ping = (ping * 3 + delta) / 4. Because it is the only timing-only packet in the play state, it is the reference clock that ping spoofers, disablers and timing-based velocity exploits all anchor on.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleKeepAlive echoes immediately: addToSendQueue(new C00PacketKeepAlive(packetIn.func_149134_c())). Server side, processKeepAlive is a pure timing check: a matching key updates the ping EMA, a wrong key is silently ignored. There is no per-connection timeout in the vanilla 1.8.9 server for a missing echo; timeouts are enforced by the network layer read timeout or by anti-cheat plugins. That asymmetry, an immediate client echo versus a server that never punishes a missing one, is what every keepalive-timing exploit depends on.

Four distinct uses in the 8 clients. (1) Debugger in Rise 5.99, 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 prints incoming keepalive ids to chat so the user can watch server cadence while tuning other modules. (2) Rise 6.2.4 WatchdogVelocity and WatchdogPredictionVelocity cancel the keepalive while a velocity spoof is armed, silencing the server's timing reference during the spoof window. (3) Sigma 4.11 Disabler Erisium mode captures the key on receive and replays a stale C00 every 1500ms, freezing the measured ping. (4) Rise 6.x NetworkAPI registers the class so JavaScript scripts can hook its receive. Note the corpus has no PingSpoof hit for S00: the spoofers in these clients intercept the C00 echo side instead.

Because the vanilla echo is immediate, any delay, cancellation or replay shows up as a ping shift or a stalled keepalive stream. The Watchdog velocity modules cancel S00 while holding S12/S32 packets so the server cannot correlate a latency spike with the velocity cancel; WatchdogPredictionVelocity re-injects the buffered keepalive on the strafe trigger to restore sequencing. Sigma's Erisium mode cancels C00 echoes and re-sends the last captured key on a timer, which keeps the server's key comparison failing silently so the ping EMA never updates. The trade-off is structural: cancellation is invisible to the packet stream but leaves the connection dead on servers that do track keepalive gaps.

implementation.overview: The clientbound keepalive, echoed instantly by vanilla and used by clients as the timing reference for ping, disabler and velocity-spoof logic. Corpus hits: Debugger (Rise 5.99/6.x), WatchdogVelocity and WatchdogPredictionVelocity (Rise 6.2.4), Sigma's Erisium disabler mode, and the Rise 6.x script NetworkAPI registry.
implementation.server_handling: NetHandlerPlayServer sends S00PacketKeepAlive(field_147378_h) roughly every second from its tick loop. processKeepAlive: if the echoed key matches field_147378_h, ping = (ping * 3 + (now - lastPingTime)) / 4; wrong or missing keys are silently dropped with no penalty. There is no vanilla timeout for a dead keepalive; connection liveness is the network layer's job.
implementation.protocol_notes: PLAY state, id 0x00, one VarInt int key (server-tick counter in vanilla). Clientbound; the serverbound echo is C00PacketKeepAlive with the same id value but a different class in the opposite direction. The key is opaque to the client: modules that mutate or replay it rely on the server never validating beyond equality with the last sent key. Because it arrives constantly, it is also the cheapest packet for modules to use as a timing beacon.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP and AAC track keepalive timing to separate real latency from timer abuse; a frozen or wildly inflated ping is a classic timer/fly tell. Verus-era checks correlate keepalive gaps with C0F transaction gaps, which is why the Rise 6.2.4 Watchdog modes cancel S00 and S32 together, and why Sigma's Erisium mode replays keys instead of cancelling outright: pure cancellation is strong but lethal on servers with keepalive timeouts. Debugger and NetworkAPI are observation-only and never flag.

modules.name: Debugger
modules.purpose: Print incoming keepalive ids to chat so the user can observe the server's keepalive cadence while developing or tuning timing-based modules.
modules.how_it_works: A PacketReceiveEvent handler checks instanceof S00PacketKeepAlive and prints 'KeepAlive | id: <key>' via Rise.addChatMessage; it prints S32PacketConfirmTransaction ids the same way. Rise 6.x gates the branch behind a keepAlive BooleanValue and formats through ChatUtil.display.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None: observation only, no wire mutation, so the vanilla echo still fires and nothing is flagged.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 Debugger.java (lines 113-114) add the keepAlive BooleanValue toggle and switch to ChatUtil.display; both still read func_149134_c() for the id.

modules.name: WatchdogVelocity / WatchdogPredictionVelocity (keepalive cancel)
modules.purpose: Cancel incoming keepalives while a velocity spoof is armed, so the server's timing probes stay silent during the window where the client holds velocity and transaction packets.
modules.how_it_works: A PacketReceiveEvent switch: while active, S12PacketEntityVelocity and S32PacketConfirmTransaction are buffered and cancelled, and the S00PacketKeepAlive case either cancels outright (WatchdogVelocity, gated by a spoof BooleanValue) or buffers it on every third tick (WatchdogPredictionVelocity). On the strafe/boost trigger the buffer is replayed through PacketUtil.receive, restoring the keepalive and transaction sequence.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Suppressing keepalive echoes during a knockback spoof prevents the server from measuring a latency spike that correlates with the velocity cancel. Cancelling S00 and S32 together keeps the two timing references consistent, which matters because Verus-style checks correlate keepalive gaps with transaction gaps.
modules.variations: WatchdogVelocity.java (line 125) cancels the keepalive without buffering it, gated by its own spoof BooleanValue and paired with S16/S15/S17 entity-look buffering; WatchdogPredictionVelocity adds the 3-tick buffering and yaw-based release logic.

modules.name: Disabler (Erisium keepalive replay)
modules.purpose: Freeze the server's ping measurement by cancelling C00 echoes and re-sending a stale captured key on a fixed 1500ms cadence.
modules.how_it_works: The EventPacket receive handler intercepts S00PacketKeepAlive, stores func_149134_c() as lastKey, and arms the erisium flag. In EventUpdate, when erisium is set and the timer hits 1500ms, the module sends C00PacketKeepAlive(lastKey) via sendPacketNoEvent. The send-side branch cancels real C00 echoes in Faithful, Erisium, SagePvP and ColdNetwork modes.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The stale key makes processKeepAlive drop the update silently, freezing ping with no packet-level anomaly. The periodic replay keeps the connection alive on servers that do track keepalive gaps, which pure cancellation cannot claim. The mode pairs with the transaction cancels in the same module (SagePvP/ColdNetwork) for servers that correlate the two.
modules.variations: No other client in the corpus implements the capture-and-replay pattern on this packet; Rise 6.x and Memeware implement the same idea on the C00 send side instead.

modules.name: NetworkAPI (script registry)
modules.purpose: Expose S00PacketKeepAlive to the JavaScript scripting API so user scripts can hook its receive event.
modules.how_it_works: A static Class array named clientbound lists S00PacketKeepAlive.class alongside every other play-state server packet; the script engine maps the registered classes to receive events for script handlers. The corresponding serverbound array lists C00PacketKeepAlive.class for the send side.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None: scripts run client-side and the registry itself never mutates packets; any flagging risk comes from what the script does with the event.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 ships the identical registry at com/alan/clients/script/api/NetworkAPI.java. No other client exposes this packet to a scripting layer.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent is the universal hook for the clientbound S00. Rise 6.x uses @EventLink listeners; Sigma uses its RegisterEvent EventPacket bus; the script path routes through NetworkAPI's class registry.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 uses per-module onPacketReceive overrides; Rise 6.x uses component and @EventLink listener APIs with PacketUtil.receive/sendNoEvent for replay; Sigma mutates nothing on receive but stores the key for its send-side replay; Spicy, Memeware, Nekoware and Tenacity have no module-level reference in this corpus.
